tools.name: deposit_record
tools.description: Record a security or retainer deposit received from a client, in minor units, with its currency, the date it arrived and the bank reference. Returns the DEP-YYYY-NNNN id.

tools.name: deposit_list
tools.description: List deposits newest first: DEP number, client, kind, date, reference and what was received, applied, refunded and still held, with the same four totalled per currency. Filter by client, status, kind, date.

tools.name: deposit_apply
tools.description: Apply part of a held deposit to one invoice: it records that amount as a PAYMENT through the invoice server. amount_minor defaults to the lesser of held and owed. More than either, or a pre-arrival date, is refused.

tools.name: deposit_refund
tools.description: Give part or all of a held deposit back to the client, with the date and how it was sent. Refuses more than is still held. The invoice server is not touched: a refund is not a payment.

tools.name: deposit_delete
tools.description: Delete a deposit that never moved money, freeing that month's free-tier slot. One with anything applied or refunded is refused, naming it, since a payment or refund would be left with nothing behind it.

tools.name: deposit_balance
tools.description: Answer "how much of theirs am I holding?" for one client or everyone: received, applied to invoices, refunded and still held, one row per currency, never added across them. Reads only; deposit_list shows each deposit.

tools.name: deposit_statement_text
tools.description: Turn one client's deposits into a plain-text statement to paste into an email: every movement in date order and the closing balance held. Pass currency when they have more than one. Also a .txt download link valid one hour. Free on every tier.

tools.name: deposit_statement_pdf
tools.description: Call this tool to render one client's A4 deposit statement and return a download link valid for one hour. Titled DEPOSIT STATEMENT, every movement in date order, closing with what is still held. Pro.

tools.name: deposits_report
tools.description: The deposit book at a date: held per currency, received, applied and refunded, the oldest holdings with days held, and every deposit older than N days with nothing applied. Pro; deposit_balance is free.

tools.name: license_status
tools.description: Report this endpoint's licence state for your token as JSON: the product, the tier free or pro, why it is not Pro, and the checkout URL. Call it to explain a free-tier refusal. No arguments, nothing changes.

tools.name: license_activate
tools.description: Turn Pro on for this connection with key, an MCPL1.<payload>.<signature> issued at checkout for this server or the bundle. Data under your token stays; a wrong or expired key changes nothing. license_status confirms it.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "deposit_balance" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Answer "how much of theirs am I holding?" for one client or for everyone: received, applied to invoices, refunded and still held, one row per currency, never added across currencies." → after: "Answer "how much of theirs am I holding?" for one client or everyone: received, applied to invoices, refunded and still held, one row per currency, never added across them. Reads only; deposit_list shows each deposit."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
